data.title: Peer Oversight in Collective Decision Making
data.description: arXiv:2608.28754v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This article introduces peer $k$-oversight, a property of sequential collective decision mechanisms requiring at least $k$ agents to be responsible for every harmful outcome. It is shown that whenever $k$-oversight can be achieved by redistributing control over the decisions in a mechanism, it can be achieved using just $k$ agents. A polynomial-time algorithm is also presented that determines whether such a redistribution exists and, when it does, constructs one. These results establish peer oversight as a tractable design principle for multiagent decision-making systems.
data.author: Sarah Mohsen, Pavel Naumov
